title: The Unfaithful Bride

questions.question: God tells Ezekiel to make known to Jerusalem her abominations. What does God say about Jerusalem's origin and birth?
options: "Your origin and your birth are of the land of the Canaanites; your father was an Amorite and your mother a Hittite."
"You were born of righteous parents, Sarah and Abraham."
"You were brought up from the land of Egypt from your youth."
"You descended from the stars of heaven."
questions.correctAnswer: "Your origin and your birth are of the land of the Canaanites; your father was an Amorite and your mother a Hittite."
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 16:3 (ESV): "Your origin and your birth are of the land of the Canaanites; your father was an Amorite and your mother a Hittite."

questions.question: On the day Jerusalem was born, what was NOT done to her?
options: Her cord was not cut, she was not washed with water, nor rubbed with salt, nor swaddled with bands
She was not given a name
She was not presented to the priest
She was not given milk and honey
questions.correctAnswer: Her cord was not cut, she was not washed with water, nor rubbed with salt, nor swaddled with bands
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 16:4 (ESV): "And as for your birth, on the day you were born your cord was not cut, nor were you washed with water to cleanse you, nor rubbed with salt, nor swaddled with bands."

questions.question: Where was the infant Jerusalem cast out?
options: On the open field, for you were abhorred
In the river, to be swept away
In the valley of Hinnom, to be burned
In the desert, to die of thirst
questions.correctAnswer: On the open field, for you were abhorred
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 16:5 (ESV): "you were cast out on the open field, for you were abhorred, on the day that you were born."

questions.question: When God passed by and saw her wallowing in her blood, what single word did He speak over her that gave her life?
options: "Live!"
"Arise!"
"Breathe!"
"Awake!"
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 16:6 (ESV): "I said to you in your blood, 'Live!' I said to you in your blood, 'Live!'"

questions.question: When Jerusalem grew up and reached the age for love, what did God do to cover her nakedness?
options: "I spread the corner of my garment over you and covered your nakedness."
"I clothed you with the skins of animals."
"I gave you a robe of righteousness."
"I covered you with leaves from the cedar."
questions.correctAnswer: "I spread the corner of my garment over you and covered your nakedness."
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 16:8 (ESV): "and I spread the corner of my garment over you and covered your nakedness; I made my vow to you and entered into a covenant with you, declares the Lord God, and you became mine."

questions.question: What fine materials did God clothe and adorn Jerusalem with?
options: Fine linen, silk, embroidered cloth, fine leather sandals, bracelets, a necklace, a ring, and a beautiful crown
Gold armor and a bronze shield
Sackcloth and ashes for humility
Feathers and precious stones from Ophir
questions.correctAnswer: Fine linen, silk, embroidered cloth, fine leather sandals, bracelets, a necklace, a ring, and a beautiful crown
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 16:10-12 (ESV): "I clothed you also with embroidered cloth and shod you with fine leather. I wrapped you in fine linen and covered you with silk. And I adorned you with ornaments... and a beautiful crown upon your head."

questions.question: What did Jerusalem trust in that led to her playing the whore?
options: Her beauty and her renown
Her strong walls
The armies of Egypt
The wealth of Solomon
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 16:15 (ESV): "But you trusted in your beauty and played the whore because of your renown and lavished your whorings on any passerby; your beauty became his."

questions.question: What detestable thing did Jerusalem do with the sons and daughters she bore to God?
options: She sacrificed them to be devoured by idols
She sold them as slaves to Babylon
She abandoned them in the open field
She married them to foreigners
questions.correctAnswer: She sacrificed them to be devoured by idols
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 16:20 (ESV): "And you took your sons and your daughters, whom you had borne to me, and these you sacrificed to them to be devoured."

questions.question: What did Jerusalem NOT remember in all her abominations and whorings?
options: The days of her youth, when she was naked and bare, wallowing in her blood
The covenant of Sinai
The plagues of Egypt
The promises to Abraham
questions.correctAnswer: The days of her youth, when she was naked and bare, wallowing in her blood
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 16:22 (ESV): "And in all your abominations and your whorings you did not remember the days of your youth, when you were naked and bare, wallowing in your blood."

questions.question: Unlike normal prostitutes, what bizarre thing did Jerusalem do regarding payment?
options: She gave gifts to all her lovers to come to her, instead of receiving payment
She cursed her lovers after taking their money
She paid them in livestock rather than gold
She only took silver, never gold
questions.correctAnswer: She gave gifts to all her lovers to come to her, instead of receiving payment
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 16:33-34 (ESV): "Men give gifts to all prostitutes, but you gave your gifts to all your lovers, bribing them to come to you from every side... giving payment while no payment was given to you;"

questions.question: Because of her unfaithfulness, who did God say He would gather against Jerusalem?
options: All your lovers with whom you took pleasure, all those you loved and all those you loathed
Only the armies of the north
The angels of destruction
The kings of the earth
questions.correctAnswer: All your lovers with whom you took pleasure, all those you loved and all those you loathed
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 16:37 (ESV): "therefore, behold, I will gather all your lovers with whom you took pleasure, all those you loved and all those you loathed. I will gather them against you from every side..."

questions.question: What proverb will men use concerning Jerusalem?
options: "Like mother, like daughter."
"A city on a hill cannot be hidden."
"The glory has departed."
"A ruined vine bears no fruit."
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 16:44 (ESV): "Behold, everyone who uses proverbs will use this proverb about you: 'Like mother, like daughter.'"

questions.question: Who are named as Jerusalem's "sisters"?
options: Samaria (the elder) and Sodom (the younger)
Babylon and Nineveh
Egypt and Assyria
Tyre and Sidon
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 16:46 (ESV): "And your elder sister is Samaria, who lived with her daughters to the north of you; and your younger sister, who lived to the south of you, is Sodom with her daughters."

questions.question: What was the specific sin of Sodom, according to Ezekiel?
options: She and her daughters had pride, excess of food, and prosperous ease, but did not aid the poor and needy
She burned children to Molech
She tore down the altars of Yahweh
She waged war against angels
questions.correctAnswer: She and her daughters had pride, excess of food, and prosperous ease, but did not aid the poor and needy
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 16:49 (ESV): "Behold, this was the guilt of your sister Sodom: she and her daughters had pride, excess of food, and prosperous ease, but did not aid the poor and needy."

questions.question: At the end of the chapter, despite all Jerusalem's sin, what does God promise to do?
options: "I will remember my covenant with you in the days of your youth, and I will establish for you an everlasting covenant."
"I will wipe you from the face of the earth permanently."
"I will make you a slave to Babylon forever."
"I will give your land to Edom."
questions.correctAnswer: "I will remember my covenant with you in the days of your youth, and I will establish for you an everlasting covenant."
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 16:60 (ESV): "yet I will remember my covenant with you in the days of your youth, and I will establish for you an everlasting covenant."

key_verse_text: "yet I will remember my covenant with you in the days of your youth, and I will establish for you an everlasting covenant."
